text:
maya-support: heads-up — Brightline (tenant-brightline) on dedicated pool dp-eu3-07 is reporting sudden p95 token latency jumps and a spike of 429s starting ~2026-11-03T03:10Z. Customer says latency goes from ~40ms to 1200ms and they see a billing jump. Attaching snippets from the edge + tenant logs below.

maya-support: logs: 
```
[2026-11-03T03:10:12Z] request_id=abc123 tenant=tenant-brightline route=/v1/generate status=429 reason="rate_limit" server=svc-infer-12
[2026-11-03T03:10:12Z] model=redwood-1 response_time_ms=1187 tokens=180
[2026-11-03T03:10:13Z] request_id=abc124 tenant=tenant-other route=/v1/embeddings status=200 response_time_ms=45
```

maya-support: customer on Dedicated (eu-west) — pool configured as fractional MIG packing (3x 1g.5 slices per GPU). Node reported in logs: node-id=gpu-eu3-node-27.

omar-sre: can you paste `nvidia-smi -L` and `nvidia-smi dmon` from that node? also need `runtimesctl describe --node gpu-eu3-node-27` so we can see slice assignments.

omar-sre: quick guess: noisy neighbor / SM saturation on one physical GPU causing other slices to see degraded tail latency.

maya-support: pasted requested outputs below (captured 03:12Z):
```
# nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (UUID: GPU-AAAA)
  MIG Device 0: 1g.5gb (UUID: MIG-GPU0-0)
  MIG Device 1: 1g.5gb (UUID: MIG-GPU0-1)
  MIG Device 2: 1g.5gb (UUID: MIG-GPU0-2)
# nvidia-smi dmon -s u
#GPU     SM   Mem   Enc   Dec  Power
   0     98    12    0     0   340
```

lee-runtime: SM 98% is huge for a MIG-packed GPU. That matches SM saturation. Need per-MIG SM utilization though — NVML should expose per-MIG metrics if MIG mode enabled; check nvmlDeviceGetMigDeviceHandleByIndex and query smUtil.

lee-runtime: mitigation suggestions:
- temporarily move tenant-brightline to an isolated slice (no co-tenants) — low-risk quick mitigation.
- bump pool min nodes to avoid autoscale thrash while we triage (min_replicas=2 -> 4).
- if workload is bursty, enable burst capacity in Dedicated plan.

sasha-eng: repro steps for infra to correlate:
1) grab a request_id from a 429 (e.g., abc123).
2) grep sidecar logs for X-Request-ID / request_id and correlate to pod and MIG device: `kubectl -n runtime logs pod/sidecar-<> | grep abc123`
3) on node: `runtimesctl trace --req abc123 --output /tmp/trace.json`
4) collect `dmesg -T | tail -n 200` and `cat /var/log/nvidia-installer.log`

sasha-eng: also can we snapshot per-tenant KV cache hit rates? If cache misses spike, tokens per request increase and can amplify load.

omar-sre: confirmed autoscaler config for dp-eu3-07: min_replicas=1, max_replicas=8, cooldown=60s. With short bursts the scaler isn't reacting fast enough -> single node becomes hot, tenants collocate. We should consider: increase min_replicas and add a short warmup window for new nodes.

team-sre-bot: [automated] Eviction planner created: node gpu-eu3-node-27 scheduled for proactive tenant shuffle at 2026-11-03T03:30Z to reduce tail latency (dry-run). Action ticket: #INC-2247.

lee-runtime: please collect `nvml` per-MIG utilization, `nvidia-smi pmon -c 1` for a 10s window and `perf stat -e cycles,instructions,cache-misses -p <pid>` on the heavy worker to confirm memory bandwidth thrash.

maya-support: copied next steps back to customer: 1) short migration to isolated slice; 2) increase pool min_replicas to 3 for 2 hours; 3) we will collect NVML dumps and escalate to runtime team if SM/memory BW confirmed.

maya-support: also flagged billing team — customer reports a surprise charge from autoscale bursts; asked billing to hold invoice pending triage.

sasha-eng: quick fallback policy to reduce 429 risk: return 503 or a smaller model (redwood-1-small) when queue depth > threshold. Example: `x-rr-fallback: model=redwood-1-small`. Adds graceful degradation while we fix infra.

omar-sre: recording evidence for postmortem: physical GPU GPU-AAAA shows sustained SM>90% coincident with request bursts from tenant-brightline. Likely noisy neighbor on same GPU (non-isolated slices). Recommend reviewing packing policy for dp-eu3-07: consider switching to 2x 1g.10gb slices or reserving whole MIG for heavy tenants.

lee-runtime: i'll take the NVML dumps and the perf traces, will triage kernel-level scheduling and preemption behavior. If we see SM hangups we'll roll a micro-rollback that disables fractional packing for that node set and force clean placement.

maya-support: thanks — will update when migration completes and when billing hold is confirmed. :thumbsup:
